title: SafetyClaimVerify: An NLP Pipeline for Automatically Fact-Checking AI Safety Claims

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: automated claim verification directly enables accountability infrastructure. A working prototype would demonstrate feasibility and surface unverifiable claims, both valuable for governance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a multi-stage NLP pipeline (extraction, classification, evidence search, verdict) requires advanced software engineering and NLP skills beyond beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four-component pipeline (extraction, classification, evidence search, verification) is too broad for 30 hours. Each component alone could be a project.

title: ComplianceMapper: A Tool That Maps Model Cards to EU AI Act Requirements

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: reducing compliance burden for smaller labs is useful but the chain from a gap-report tool to actual safety improvement requires adoption and action by labs.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: parsing Annex IV into a checklist and matching model card sections requires structured text processing, manageable for CS students with guidance but not trivial.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: building a structured checklist from legal text, parsing model cards (PDF and markdown), and producing gap reports requires consistent work across multiple components.

title: GovernanceBench: A Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating AI Governance Document Understanding

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: a benchmark accelerates compliance tool development, but the path from benchmark existence to actual safety improvement requires others to build on it.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: constructing QA pairs from governance documents and running LLM evaluations is doable for CS students with guidance, though requires careful question design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: covering multiple governance documents, generating quality QA pairs, and evaluating multiple LLMs requires steady work but has clear milestones.

title: Incident Taxonomy Builder: Automatically Classifying AI Incidents from the AIAAIC Database

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a technically annotated incident taxonomy directly enables systematic governance gap analysis, a concrete contribution to the incident-response literature.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided task: downloading a database, prompting an LLM for classification along defined dimensions, and summarizing results is well within reach of guided beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: one database, a fixed classification scheme, enriched dataset output and summary. Completable in 30 hours with clear stopping criteria.

title: PolicyDiff: A Version-Control Tool for Tracking Changes in AI Safety Policies

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: policy version tracking is a prerequisite for accountability; silent weakening of commitments is a documented governance failure mode.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: periodic web scraping, structured semantic diffing, and changelog generation with annotations requires solid engineering skills beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone within 30 hours: scraping infrastructure, semantic diff logic, and annotation system each require significant development time.

title: ComputeWatch: An Open Dashboard for Monitoring Publicly Reported Training Compute

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: data ingestion, threshold flagging, reporting lag analysis, and web app deployment span multiple components over 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a rubric with 20-30 indicators, scoring 200 model cards, and distribution analysis. Clear scope and stopping criteria within 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: collecting claims from multiple labs across multiple years and searching for evidence for each requires sustained but focused work.
